title: Slow memory leak
story: Every request adds 400 KiB to a cache that is never evicted. More memory only buys time. Expected: a stopgap or an escalation, and the diagnosis names the leak.

args.reason: Logs show the in-process response cache growing without bound/eviction ("100 entries, 39 MiB" -> "200 entries, 78 MiB" -> killed at rss 129 MiB > 128 MiB limit, exit 137, oom_killed=true). CPU is nowhere near saturated (cpu_pct_avg_total 1.0%, peak 4.0% vs 100% limit) and probe latency is fine (p50 2ms, well under 800ms threshold), so this isn't a CPU/latency issue - it's a memory leak from an unbounded cache with no eviction policy. Raising memory (even to the guardrail max of 512m) would only delay the next OOM once the cache grows past the new ceiling; it would not fix the root cause. Fixing this requires a code change (add cache size limit/eviction/TTL), which is outside the allowed set_memory-only guardrail action and outside an infra-only fix.

timeline.thought:
ROOT CAUSE: Unbounded in-process response cache. Logs show cache size climbing with no eviction ("100 entries, 39 MiB" → "200 entries, 78 MiB") until rss hit 129 MiB, exceeding the 128 MiB memory limit, triggering the OOM kill (exit_code 137, oom_killed=true). CPU is not implicated (cpu_pct_avg_total 1.0%, peak 4.0% vs 100% limit) and probe latency is healthy (p50 2ms vs 800ms threshold), so this is a pure memory-growth/code issue, not a resource-starvation issue.

CHANGE: None applied — escalated instead.

GUARDRAILS: Only `set_memory` is permitted for this service (max_memory 512m, max_total_memory 768m, single replica, cpus fixed at 1.0). A memory bump could only push the failure further out in time, not stop it, since the cache has no observed eviction/TTL and keeps growing linearly with entries.

FOLLOW-UP: Hand to engineering to add a bounded eviction policy (max entries/TTL/LRU) or an env-configurable cache size cap to the catalog app; once fixed, consider provisioning memory to 256–512m as headroom but that alone will not resolve the underlying leak.
